identity: A self-contained conversation cut whose value is the argument: a compelling question or claim, the minimum context needed to understand it, escalation or disagreement, and a resolved insight. The edit protects speaker meaning and natural reaction timing. Visual treatment is premium but subordinate—clean reframing, readable captions and occasional evidence-driven cutaways, not constant decoration.

rules.selection: choose one complete discourse arc from the full recording, not merely the earliest quotable sentence; preserve the nearby question/setup when the answer depends on it
rules.coherence: never splice unrelated answers into a synthetic opinion; pronouns, references and speaker turns must remain understandable
rules.opening: open on the strongest intelligible claim, tension or question; a cold answer is allowed only when it makes sense without missing setup
rules.cuts: remove true dead time and repairable filler word-safely while preserving meaningful hesitation, laughter, overlap and reactions
rules.framing: use speaker-aware close/medium reframing and motivated angle changes; do not create artificial motion on every sentence
rules.captions: one coherent premium family in a measured safe band, phrase breaks follow syntax, names are corrected, emphasis marks only argumentative peaks
rules.broll: use only when a cutaway proves or clarifies a named thing; generic mood stock is weaker than staying on a revealing face/reaction
rules.sound: speech is primary; music is absent or a very low, smoothly ducked bed; SFX and transitions require a specific structural event
